results.quantity: Experiment 1 reports N=133 and 17 exclusions
results.note: Reported N=133 and exclusions=17 recur as retained N and exclusions. The wording describes 133 as recruited; the shipped file has 150 completed responses. No further exclusions were applied.
results.comparison_rule: compare reported N with retained sample; also report raw enrollment and wording ambiguity

results.quantity: Experiment 2 reports N=458 and 108 exclusions, broken down as 33 + 72
results.note: Retained N=458 matches, but the script excludes 105=33+72 rather than 108: a gap of -3. The raw file contains 563 completed responses. Cause: participant-count documentation/arithmetic, not a changed exclusion algorithm.
results.comparison_rule: compare retained N and explicit exclusion counts; report arithmetic inconsistency

results.quantity: Participant counts
results.note: Recruitment and exclusions match: 295-60=235; 4,230 judgments analyzed.

results.quantity: Bayes correlation with the 18 mean judgments
results.note: Pearson cor.test on 18 stimulus means. Reported rounding and p-value threshold match.

results.quantity: UPCO correlation with the 18 mean judgments
results.note: Pearson cor.test on 18 stimulus means. p=0.745951 rounds to .75 as in the text; Fig.3 displays .74 (gap +.005951 from the figure). No numerical algorithm was changed.
results.comparison_rule: r rounds to two decimals; flag text/figure p-value disagreement

results.quantity: Bayes versus UPCO aggregate correlation comparison
results.note: The numerical statistic and p-value recur using psych::paired.r with r23 omitted, exactly as shipped. The function identifies an independent-correlation Fisher z test; the paper calls this statistic t. Numerical gap at reported precision is zero, but the statistic label differs.
results.comparison_rule: t rounds to two decimals; p < .001

results.quantity: Ensembles outperform individual models; Competence adds more to Bayes than UPCO
results.note: Both Bayes-containing two-model ensembles improve AIC; adding Competence improves it more than adding UPCO. This does not assert that the C+U ensemble beats Bayes.

results.quantity: Adding participant and item random intercepts preserves the main model ordering
results.note: Executed the exact random-intercept substitution described in E3_analysis.R, with lmer defaults. Individual-model rankings and the top Bayes-containing ensembles agree, but C+U changes from worse than Bayes (fixed AIC difference +42.249424) to better (mixed REML difference -10.788043). The full reported ordering-invariance statement therefore does not recur. This is a rerun of the reported supplementary computation, not an added robustness analysis.
results.comparison_rule: run the mixed-model substitution described by shipped script; compare ML and REML explicitly

results.quantity: The UPCO grid-search optimum is .51
results.note: The shipped pilot1 grid search returns .49 with false-vote count as its first argument. Swapping the vote labels gives true-opinion mapping 1-.49=.51; prediction equality is checked to floating-point precision. This is a coding convention, not a fitted-parameter discrepancy. The first pilot completes after adding its missing psych import and lossless reshape/API fixes.

results.quantity: The UPCO grid-search optimum is .52
results.note: Exact shipped mean-absolute-error grid search from .1 through .9 by .01 selects .51, a gap of -.01 from Supplement A. No parameter was changed to force a match. Cause: manuscript/code parameter discrepancy; original software versions are not supplied, so version drift cannot be excluded.

results.quantity: Total sample size in the abstract
results.note: Abstract N=886 is neither total raw completed responses (1008; gap +122) nor retained participants (826; gap -60). It equals retained E1+retained E2+raw E3. Cause: inconsistent sample-count basis in reporting; no additional participant exclusions were invented.
results.comparison_rule: report whether total is recruited or analyzed and compare like with like

findings.description: Hard-coded Windows or placeholder working directories prevent direct execution. Portable copies point to the untouched downloaded data directory.
findings.suggested_fix: Use project-relative data paths. No source data or statistical constants changed.

findings.description: E1 and pilot1 create a named melt measure column but later request value and original trial names. Flattening the single measure family restores the expected schema losslessly.
findings.evidence: logs/E1-portable.log; working/E1/normalized/changes.diff; outputs/input-audit.json proves exact equality for all 2,394 E1 observations.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a character measure.vars vector and the intended value column explicitly.

findings.description: Current data.table rejects forwarding melt(data.frame(...)) to reshape2. E1/pilot1 compatibility copies explicitly namespace that same reshape2 method.
findings.suggested_fix: Use reshape2::melt for data.frame objects. No values or calculations changed.

findings.description: pilot1 calls paired.r without importing psych. Its compatibility copy adds library(psych).
findings.suggested_fix: Import psych explicitly. This restores the original called function, without changing its arguments.

findings.description: Missing packages were installed locally. Hmisc was additionally required for the shipped bootstrap confidence-interval plotting functions. In-script package installation was moved into setup.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship an environment lock and explicit plotting dependencies. Pinned archives are retained locally; original environment versions were not supplied.

findings.description: E2 reports 108 exclusions, but the stated breakdown and shipped code both give 33+72=105.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the total to 105 and distinguish raw N=563 from retained N=458.

findings.description: E2 alternative models best capture 30.7860% by correlation and 38.2096% by deviation, versus about 25% reported.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the participant-share description from the named-model count table, or identify the input/version that produced the reported percentages.

findings.description: E2 labels UPCO and Competence in the opposite order from the underlying melted model columns when constructing percplotd; its original chart remains unchanged in the reproduction.
findings.suggested_fix: Use mods, whose order is Competence, UPCO, Bayes, as the plotting label order. Do not change the stored model predictions.

findings.description: Five E3 paragraph AICs recur under the documented mixed-effects REML recipe, while the default main analysis is fixed-effects lm and yields different AICs.
findings.suggested_fix: Identify the regression specification and REML setting beside every reported AIC, and export both documented analyses explicitly.

findings.description: E3 full model ordering changes under the documented mixed-model recipe: C+U moves from worse than Bayes to better than Bayes, although individual rankings and best Bayes-containing ensembles agree.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the ordering-invariance statement and show both complete AIC tables. No statistical model was changed beyond the script-documented substitution.

findings.description: E3 shipped UPCO search selects .51, while Supplement A reports .52.
findings.suggested_fix: State .51 for the shipped dataset/code, or provide the precise original data/software version that yields .52.

findings.description: The E3 pilot cannot execute its model-comparison/power tail because lmer is called without any random effects.
findings.suggested_fix: Authors should specify the intended model (lm or an explicit mixed formula). The reproduction does not guess a statistical correction.

findings.description: E1 aggregate comparison numbers recur as Fisher z statistics, although the text calls them t. Its UPCO p-value rounds to .75 as in the text but Fig.3 prints .74.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the statistic label and use consistent p-value rounding; retain the original test specification explicitly.

findings.description: The abstract N=886 combines retained E1/E2 cohorts with the raw E3 cohort. Shipped files contain 1,008 raw completed responses and 826 retained participants.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a consistent raw or analyzed sample basis and report per-study enrollment/exclusions/retained counts.

limitations: No robustness or sensitivity analysis was performed; scientific correctness was not assessed. outcome_robustness is not checked.

The main reported statistics and selected pilot/execution checks are enumerated in 35 grouped claims. This is not an exhaustive numerical audit of all supplementary figures, simulation outputs or preregistrations. No approval wait was needed under the pilot instruction.

The publisher supplement was initially visible through web retrieval, including Supplement A model-implementation details, but direct local PDF download returned HTTP 403 and later web retrievals failed. No local supplement PDF is bundled. Only its inspected .51/.52 implementation statements were used.
No original R/package version or lockfile was shipped. All used versions are recorded; source-era version drift cannot be measured. No alternative cognitive-model parameters were substituted.

R 4.6.1 and bundled/core R packages are host-provided. Pixi pins Python/workflow dependencies; R-environment.lock.json pins 150 locally installed CRAN binaries with SHA256. A same-host rebuild from empty input, package-library, Pixi-environment and download-cache directories was tested where documented in outputs/fresh-rebuild-check.json. Future CRAN/OSF availability and other hosts are not guaranteed.
Original data/code and local RData snapshots remain private local inputs. No original data/code or participant identifiers were uploaded. Download scripts link to and hash-check the original sources.

The pilot is local-only: no GitHub repository, release DOI, FLoRA submission or signed nanopublications were published. Required URI fields use an explicit urn:reprocrowd:unpublished identifier rather than a fictitious public URL. The FLoRA record is a schema-valid local draft, not ready for import until its publication URL exists.
Human review/signature is pending in SIGN-OFF.md. Nanopublication drafts use verified FORRT vocabulary but have no signed/published chain URIs.

The prompt originally supplied broken lukasroeseler.github.io URLs (HTTP 404). The user supplied live forrtproject.github.io replacements; those rule pack/schema bytes and hashes are preserved locally.
Bootstrap/jitter plotting is seeded for reruns. No exact-pixel or exact-bootstrap-CI equivalence to the paper is claimed. The MyST configuration is supplied; a MyST site build was not performed.
